sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive the product as a premium, health‑enhancing solution that addresses specific concerns such as taste, safety, or convenience. Who benefits: Health‑conscious consumers who currently rely on bottled water or prefer a premium water experience.. Why behaviour changes: If Aquaporin positions its membrane as a high‑performance, easy‑to‑use purifier that eliminates taste concerns and provides clear health benefits, consumers will shift from bottled water to a single, reliable home unit.. How value is captured: Premium pricing for a differentiated unit, subscription services for maintenance, and brand extension into lifestyle segments.. Assumptions: Consumers currently avoid tap water due to taste or safety concerns.; A premium positioning can overcome these barriers.; Aquaporin can scale production and distribution to meet demand.. Predictions: Surveyed consumers will indicate willingness to pay at least 20% more for a membrane that promises superior taste and health benefits.; Pilot sales of a differentiated unit will show higher conversion rates than standard membranes.; Brand perception surveys will rank the differentiated unit higher than current offerings..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive the product as a convenient, low‑maintenance solution that reduces the hassle of bottled water or other alternative water sources. Who benefits: Busy households and consumers who currently spend time and money on bottled water, delivery services, or other water alternatives.. Why behaviour changes: If Aquaporin offers a membrane that is easy to install, requires minimal maintenance (e.g., cartridge replacement indicator), and integrates with smart home systems, consumers will switch from the hassle of bottled water to a single, self‑s. How value is captured: Lower upfront cost compared to premium membrane, subscription services for maintenance, and data‑driven insights that enhance convenience through smart home integration.. Assumptions: Consumers currently find bottled water delivery inconvenient or expensive.; A low‑maintenance membrane reduces perceived effort.; Smart home compatibility can be marketed as a convenience benefit.. Predictions: Surveyed consumers will rank convenience as a top reason for choosing a membrane over bottled water.; Pilot sales of a differentiated unit will show higher repeat purchase rates than standard membranes.; Pilot units will achieve higher adoption rates in households with children or elderly members..

Test "Membrane Preference Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online choice-based conjoint survey with simulated purchase decision.. Sample: 500 Danish consumers recruited via panel, balanced for age, gender, and household income. Randomly assigned to see a premium positioning message (T1) or a convenience positioning message (T2).. Measure: 1) Willingness to pay (WTP) for a differentiated membrane (e.g., premium price vs. low‑upfront cost). 2) Primary reason for choosing membrane vs. bottled water (open‑ended).. Predictions: T1: Higher WTP for premium membrane when shown taste/safety claims; primary reason will be health/quality.; T2: Higher WTP for low‑upfront‑cost membrane when shown convenience claims; primary reason will be convenience.. Decision rule: If WTP for premium membrane exceeds WTP for low‑upfront‑cost membrane by ≥20% and the primary reason for premium is health/quality, proceed to develop premium consumer proposition. If convenience reason is the primary reason for low‑upfront. Cost: 15000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions the membrane as a premium, health‑enhancing solution addressing taste, safety, and convenience concerns. Begin with a limited pilot in a niche segment (e.g., health‑conscious households) to test demand and willingness to pay before broader rollout. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: Simulated evidence SYN-AQP-UPDATE does not address T1; it concerns a maintenance-convenience proposition test and does not provide data on consumer willingness to pay for a premium positioning. New claim: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive the product as a premium, health‑enhancing solution that addresses specific concerns such as taste, safety, or convenience.. Evidence: SYN-AQP-UPDATE.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition that positions the membrane as a premium, health‑enhancing solution addressing taste, safety, and convenience concerns. Begin with a limited pilot in a niche segment (e.g., health‑conscious households) to test demand and willingness to pay before broader rollout. Target customer: Health‑conscious consumers who currently rely on bottled water or prefer a premium water experience, particularly in markets where tap water quality is perceived as uncertain.. Value proposition: A differentiated membrane that delivers superior taste, safety, and health benefits, supported by clear information and a single, reliable home unit, enabling premium pricing and subscription services for maintenance.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Membrane Preference Test (conjoint survey) to measure willingness to pay for premium positioning versus low‑upfront‑cost convenience positioning. Use the decision rule to decide whether to proceed with premium development.. Uncertainty: The size of the premium‑positioning market and the actual willingness to pay for health benefits are unknown. Evidence of strong consumer demand for premium water is limited to external studies and company claims, which may not reflect real. Would change if: If the survey shows that convenience is the primary driver of purchase and willingness to pay for premium positioning is below 20% of the low‑upfront‑cost option, we would abandon premium development and focus on a low‑maintenance, low‑cost; If new public data shows rapid growth in bottled water sales or strong consumer preference for tap water, we would reconsider the premium proposition and explore alternative routes to market.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 120 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 60 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive the product as a premium, health‑enhancing solution that addresses specific concerns such as taste, safety, or convenience. Who benefits: Health‑conscious consumers who currently rely on bottled water or prefer a premium water experience.. Why behaviour changes: If Aquaporin positions its membrane as a high‑performance, easy‑to‑use purifier that eliminates taste concerns and provides clear health benefits, consumers will shift from bottled water to a single, reliable home unit.. How value is captured: Premium pricing for a differentiated unit, subscription services for maintenance, and brand extension into lifestyle segments.. Assumptions: Consumers currently avoid tap water due to taste or safety concerns.; A premium positioning can overcome these barriers.; Aquaporin can scale production and distribution to meet demand.. Predictions: Surveyed consumers will indicate willingness to pay at least 20% more for a membrane that promises superior taste and health benefits.; Pilot sales of a differentiated unit will show higher conversion rates than standard membranes.; Brand perception surveys will rank the differentiated unit higher than current offerings..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive the product as a convenient, low‑maintenance solution that reduces the hassle of bottled water or other alternative water sources. Who benefits: Busy households and consumers who currently spend time and money on bottled water, delivery services, or other water alternatives.. Why behaviour changes: If Aquaporin offers a membrane that is easy to install, requires minimal maintenance (e.g., cartridge replacement indicator), and integrates with smart home systems, consumers will switch from the hassle of bottled water to a single, self‑s. How value is captured: Lower upfront cost compared to premium membrane, subscription services for maintenance, and data‑driven insights that enhance convenience through smart home integration.. Assumptions: Consumers currently find bottled water delivery inconvenient or expensive.; A low‑maintenance membrane reduces perceived effort.; Smart home compatibility can be marketed as a convenience benefit.. Sample: 500 adult consumers in Denmark and Germany, recruited via panel, balanced for age, gender, and household income.. Decision rule: If the premium scenario's WTP exceeds the low‑maintenance scenario's WTP by at least 15% for at least 60% of participants, proceed to develop a differentiated premium proposition. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 household washing-machine buyers eligible for the same professional-derived washer offer were assigned equally to two descriptions. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 household washing-machine buyers eligible for the same professional-derived washer offer were assigned equally to two descriptions. Both descriptions showed the same machine, brand, price, warranty, availability, service terms and verified specifications. One emphasized durability and repairability; the other emphasized washing performance and the upfront price. No discount or extra service was added. The outcome was a paid, refundable purchase reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned buyers per arm. There were 72 reservations in the durability-and-repairability description arm and 32 in the performance-and-price description arm. This tests the incremental effect of the description in this recruited population, not actual appliance lifetime, delivery capability, market size, profitability or sustained repurchase. A weaker result would not refute a different channel or product theory.

T1: Homeowners will adopt consumer‑operated laundry solutions if they perceive them as convenient and cost‑effective, leading to higher purchase rates and repeat purchases. Who benefits: Electrolux Professional Group gains revenue from consumer sales and can capture value through premium pricing and recurring service contracts.. Why behaviour changes: Growing home‑laundry market and consumer demand for commercial‑quality products create an opportunity for a consumer‑focused offering that addresses homeowner pain points such as space constraints and cost.. How value is captured: Electrolux can sell directly to consumers via online channels, retail partnerships, or wholesale to retailers, and capture value through higher margins on consumer units and service revenue.. Assumptions: Homeowners are willing to purchase commercial‑grade laundry equipment for home use.; Consumer pricing is acceptable compared to professional pricing.; Distribution channels (online, retail) can reach target homeowners effectively.. Predictions: A test offering a consumer‑oriented self‑service unit will achieve at least 5% conversion rate among homeowners who express intent to purchase.; Average transaction value will be at least 20% above the price of a comparable professional unit.; Repeat purchase rate within 12 months will be at least 15% for customers who initially purchase..

T2: Small businesses and gyms will adopt consumer‑operated laundry solutions if they need affordable, space‑efficient equipment that reduces labor costs and downtime, leading to higher adoption rates and repeat purchases. Who benefits: Electrolux Professional Group gains consumer sales revenue and can capture value through lower unit margins but higher volume and service contracts.. Why behaviour changes: Small businesses and gyms face budget constraints and need equipment that minimizes downtime; consumer‑operated units address these needs by offering compact, low‑cost solutions that can be managed by staff or users.. How value is captured: Electrolux can sell directly to consumers via online or retail channels, and capture value through recurring service contracts and volume sales, leveraging its professional expertise to ensure reliability.. Assumptions: Small businesses and gyms are willing to purchase consumer‑grade equipment for non‑professional use.; Affordable pricing is acceptable compared to professional units.; Distribution channels can reach these segments effectively.. Predictions: A test offering a consumer‑oriented unit to small businesses will achieve at least 8% conversion rate among those who express intent to purchase.; Average transaction value will be at least 15% above the price of a comparable professional unit.; Repeat purchase rate within 12 months will be at least 12% for customers who initially purchase..

Test "Consumer vs Small Business Intent Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase offer and willingness-to-pay (WTP) questions.. Sample: 500 respondents: 250 homeowners (via residential email list) and 250 small businesses/gyms (via trade association and social media).. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: "Would buy" vs "Would not buy") and WTP (price range in euros).. Predictions: T1: Homeowners will have higher purchase intent and WTP than small businesses, with a conversion rate of at least 5% among homeowners and at least 8% among small businesses.; T2: Small businesses will have higher purchase intent and WTP than homeowners, with a conversion rate of at least 8% among small businesses and at least 5% among homeowners.. Decision rule: If homeowners conversion ≥5% and small businesses conversion <8%, recommend consumer proposition for homeowners (T1). If small businesses conversion ≥8% and homeowners conversion <5%, recommend consumer proposition for small businesses (T2). Cost: 12000 euros, 8 weeks.

Target customer: Homeowners in multi‑family buildings, student housing, and other residential settings who need reliable, commercial‑grade laundry equipment for home use.. Value proposition: A consumer‑oriented, space‑efficient self‑service unit that delivers professional‑grade washing and drying performance, enabling residents to manage their own laundry with minimal downtime and cost.. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer vs Small Business Intent Test (500 respondents, 8‑week survey) to validate purchase intent and willingness to pay among homeowners and small businesses. Use the results to decide whether to proceed with a full‑f‑. Uncertainty: The size of the residential market and the price sensitivity of homeowners are uncertain. The test will clarify whether homeowners are willing to pay a premium for durability and repairability, which is central to T1.. Would change if: If the test shows homeowners conversion ≥ 5% and small businesses conversion <8%, we would shift focus to a consumer‑focused proposition for small businesses (T2).; If the test shows small businesses conversion ≥ 8% and homeowners conversion <5%, we would reconsider the consumer proposition and explore other segments.; If new evidence shows that residential demand is much smaller than expected or that small‑business demand is already high, we would abandon the consumer proposition and focus on existing professional segments.. T1: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer proposition because they value convenience, health benefits, and modern design, leading them to purchase premium, smart appliances. Who benefits: Home cooks seeking efficient, health-conscious cooking solutions.. Why behaviour changes: If the appliance is marketed as a time-saving, steam‑based cooking system that also offers health benefits (e.g., lower oil use, even cooking), home cooks will shift from traditional methods to a premium, smart device.. How value is captured: RATIONAL can capture value by pricing the product at a premium, selling through retail channels, and offering subscription services for software updates or maintenance.. Assumptions: Home cooks are willing to pay a premium for convenience and health benefits.; Retail distribution channels exist for RATIONAL products in residential markets.; Marketing can effectively communicate the convenience and health benefits to target consumers.. Predictions: In a test offering a differentiated home‑cook combi‑steamer at a 20% premium over a standard model, purchase intent among target consumers will be at least 15% higher than a baseline model without premium positioning.; Surveyed consumers will cite convenience and health benefits as primary reasons for purchase..

T2: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer proposition because they seek professional‑grade performance and reliability, leading them to purchase premium, high‑end appliances. Who benefits: Home cooks who value consistent results, ease of use, and the reputation of a professional‑grade brand.. Why behaviour changes: If the appliance is marketed as a reliable, high‑performance tool that delivers consistent results and is backed by a professional brand, home cooks will shift from generic appliances to a premium, trusted product.. T1: Home barista culture will drive demand for compact, entry‑level espresso machines that fit small spaces, creating a consumer segment willing to pay a premium for convenience. Who benefits: Home baristas seeking consistent espresso at home; Simonelli Group would capture value through premium pricing and brand association with quality coffee.. Why behaviour changes: The pandemic reinforced the home barista lifestyle, and consumers now view espresso as a daily ritual rather than a professional tool. They seek equipment that fits their living spaces and offers consistent results.. How value is captured: Simonelli can sell compact models under its Victoria Arduino brand at a higher margin, leveraging its reputation for professional-grade machines to justify premium pricing.. Assumptions: Home barista participation rates will remain stable or increase in target markets.; Consumers will allocate discretionary spending to coffee equipment despite overall market slowdown.; Simonelli can produce compact models without compromising performance.. Predictions: If a test offers a compact Victoria Arduino model to 500 home baristas, purchase intent will exceed 30% and average order value will be at least €200.; Sales of compact models will grow faster than overall consumer coffee equipment sales in the same period..

T2: Professional coffee shop operators will adopt compact, entry‑level espresso machines to reduce space requirements and lower operational costs, creating a consumer segment willing to pay for efficiency. Who benefits: Coffee shops seeking to optimize space and costs; Simonelli Group would capture value through volume sales of compact models and brand association with cost‑effective professional solutions.. Why behaviour changes: Shop owners face space constraints and rising rental costs, prompting them to seek equipment that fits smaller premises. They view compact machines as a way to maintain espresso quality without large investments.. How value is captured: Simonelli can sell compact models at a lower price point than premium professional machines, leveraging its reputation for reliability to attract cost‑conscious buyers and achieve higher unit volume.. Assumptions: Coffee shop operators will prioritize space‑saving equipment when evaluating new purchases.; There is a measurable willingness to pay for compact machines compared to standard professional models.; Simonelli can produce compact models without compromising performance.. Predictions: If a test offers a compact Victoria Arduino model to 200 coffee shops, purchase intent will exceed 25% and average order value will be at least €150.; Sales of compact models will grow faster than overall consumer coffee equipment sales in the same period..

Test "Consumer vs. Professional Purchase Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online choice-based conjoint survey with simulated purchase decision. Participants view two product concepts (Victoria Arduino compact model vs. standard Victoria Arduino model) and indicate purchase intent on a 7-point scale and maximum willingness to pay (WTP). They also state primary purchase driver (home barista convenience vs. shop space efficiency).. Sample: 500 participants: 250 self-identified home baristas (via coffeeGeek forum) and 250 professional coffee shop owners (via industry directory). Randomly assigned to view one product concept.. Measure: Purchase intent score (1–10) and WTP (in euros). Secondary measure: primary driver (binary).. Predictions: T1: Home baristas will show higher purchase intent and WTP for the compact model than shop owners, and will cite convenience as primary driver.; T2: Shop owners will show higher purchase intent and WTP for the compact model than home baristas, and will cite space efficiency as primary driver.. Decision rule: If the average purchase intent for the compact model among home baristas exceeds that for shop owners by at least 1.5 points and the WTP difference is ≥ €50, proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition for home baristas. If the. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home baristas, starting with a compact, entry-level espresso machine under the Victoria Arduino brand. Use the proposed purchase test to validate demand before full launch. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: Simulated warehouse test (SYN-D) concerns packing errors and does not address consumer demand for compact machines, so it does not affect T1. New claim: Home barista culture will drive demand for compact, entry-level espresso machines that fit small spaces, creating a consumer segment willing to pay a premium for convenience.. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home baristas, starting with a compact, entry-level espresso machine under the Victoria Arduino brand. Use the proposed purchase test to validate demand before full launch. Target customer: Home baristas who consume coffee at home and seek consistent espresso at home.. Value proposition: A compact, entry-level Victoria Arduino model that fits small spaces, offers professional-grade performance, and is priced at a premium reflecting quality and convenience, leveraging Simonelli’s reputation for premium coffee equipment.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed 10‑week, €18,000 purchase test with 500 participants (250 home baristas, 250 shop owners) to measure purchase intent and willingness to pay for the compact model versus a standard model.. Uncertainty: The size of the home barista market and their willingness to pay a premium for compact machines; the impact of overall consumer coffee equipment market slowdown; Simonelli’s ability to produce compact models without compromising performance. Would change if: If the test shows purchase intent for the compact model among home baristas is at least 1.5 points lower than among shop owners, or if WTP differences are insufficient to justify investment, we would reconsider the consumer proposition and; If new evidence shows a sustained recovery in consumer coffee equipment demand or a shift in home barista participation rates, we would reassess the need for a differentiated consumer offering.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 60 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 120 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. case.question: Should RATIONAL develop a differentiated proposition for home cooks, building on its commercial combi-steamer technology, or stay with professional kitchens? What evidence would justify either choice?

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 32 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 72 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

Test "Home Cooks Preference Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online choice-based conjoint survey with two product variants: a differentiated combi-steamer (premium convenience) and a standard steamer (control). Participants see a product description and are asked to rank importance of convenience, health/sustainability, price, and willingness to pay a premium. They then indicate purchase intent (1-7).. Sample: 300 German home cooks (18-65) recruited via an online panel, balanced for gender and age.. Measure: Primary outcome: average weighted score for convenience vs. sustainability. Secondary: willingness to pay premium (difference in price sensitivity).. Predictions: T1: Higher average score for convenience than for sustainability.; T2: Higher average score for sustainability than for convenience.. Decision rule: If the difference in average scores between convenience and sustainability is ≥ 1.5 points, proceed to develop a differentiated home‑cook proposition emphasizing convenience. If the difference is ≤ 1.5 points, maintain focus on professional. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Develop a differentiated home‑cook proposition that emphasizes convenience and premium quality, leveraging RATIONAL’s existing brand and market position in professional kitchens. Use the combi‑steamer technology as a premium, single‑device solution for home cooks, sold through specialty retailers and direct‑to‑consumer channels. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: Simulated evidence SYN-RATIONAL-UPDATE does not address home cook demand, convenience, or premium pricing; it concerns installation coordination friction and does not affect T1. New claim: Home cooks will adopt a differentiated combi-steamer if they perceive it as a premium, convenience-enhancing appliance that reduces cooking time and effort, and are willing to pay a premium price.. Evidence: SYN-RATIONAL-UPDATE.

Recommendation: Develop a differentiated home‑cook proposition that emphasizes convenience and premium quality, leveraging RATIONAL’s existing brand and market position in professional kitchens. Use the combi‑steamer technology as a premium, single‑device solution for home cooks, sold through specialty retailers and direct‑to‑consumer channels. Target customer: German home cooks (18–65) who value time‑saving, high‑quality cooking and are willing to pay a premium for convenience.. Value proposition: A compact, smart combi‑steamer that combines steaming, boiling, and cooking in one device, offering rapid meal preparation and professional‑grade results, sold at a premium price through trusted retailers.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Home Cooks Preference Test (conjoint survey) to measure willingness to pay for convenience versus sustainability. If the convenience premium exceeds 1.5 points, proceed to develop the differentiated home‑cook proposition;. Uncertainty: The size of the home‑cook market and the actual willingness to pay for convenience are uncertain. The test will resolve this, but current market data only shows B2B customers and does not reveal home‑cook demand.. Would change if: If the test shows the sustainability premium exceeds 1.5 points, we would shift focus to a health‑focused proposition emphasizing eco‑friendly features.; If the test yields no significant premium for convenience, we would reconsider the entire home‑cook expansion and stay focused on professional kitchens.. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited home cooks considering the same professional-derived combi-steamer were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed identical equipment, brand, cooking specifications, total installed price, warranty, available delivery dates and eventual plumbing/electrical work. One offer bundled an installation coordinator and a site-readiness checklist; the other required the purchaser to arrange the same qualified installers directly. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. All recruited homes were eligible for the stated installation work. The outcome was a paid refundable reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned households per arm. There were 72 reservations for the coordinated-installation offer and 32 for the purchaser-arranged offer. This tests whether coordination friction changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show that the appliance fits ordinary kitchens, eliminates drain or power requirements, earns a margin, or justifies diverting resources from professional customers. It does not establish market size or a need for new RATIONAL hardware. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow coordination mechanism changes.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 households already using a compatible drinking-water purifier received the same membrane specifications, water-quality information, brand, warranty and total annual price. Half were offered a prepaid plan with scheduled cartridge delivery and replacement reminders; half were offered a prepaid self-service cartridge plan without that delivery schedule or reminders. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid plan enrollment remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned households per arm. This what-if assumes an authorised operator can legally supply and service the offer; it does not change the dossier evidence about Aquaporin's insolvency or financing. There were 60 plan enrollments in the scheduled-delivery-and-reminder plan arm and 120 in the self-service cartridge plan arm. This tests willingness to enroll in a maintenance offer under that conditional supply assumption, not membrane efficacy, correct long-term filter use, market size, company solvency or Aquaporin's ability to fund an offer. An unchanged business recommendation can be justified by those other constraints.

In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 home espresso enthusiasts considering the same Simonelli single-group machine were assigned equally to two offers. Machine, brand, price, warranty, availability and total contact time were identical. One offer included a structured hands-on home-barista setup lesson; the other included an equal-length product-specification orientation without a skill lesson. There were no discounts. The outcome was a paid, refundable machine reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned enthusiasts per arm. There were 32 reservations in the home-barista-lesson offer arm and 72 in the product-specification-orientation offer arm. This tests the incremental effect of this learning offer among recruited enthusiasts, not a need for a new machine, demand among ordinary coffee drinkers, commercial margins or lasting skill retention. It does not show that every hobby or status mechanism is true or false.

Test "Consumer vs Professional Messaging Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated product launch. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two messaging conditions: (A) premium, home-barista focus (emphasizing quality, social experience, and personal enjoyment) or (B) professional, shop-focused (emphasizing brand prestige, professional standards, and shop compatibility). Participants view a product description of a new consumer espresso machine (e.g., compact, easy. Sample: 400 participants: 200 assigned to Condition A, 200 assigned to Condition B. Recruit via coffee enthusiast panels and social media to ensure diversity in age, gender, and coffee consumption habits.. Measure: Primary measure: average stated willingness to pay (WTP) in euros. Secondary measures: purchase intent (binary: would buy), brand perception (Likert scale), and intent to recommend to peers.. Predictions: T1: Higher WTP and purchase intent in Condition A (home-barista messaging) than in Condition B.; T2: Higher WTP and purchase intent in Condition B (professional messaging) than in Condition A.. Decision rule: If the difference in average WTP between the two conditions is at least €20 (indicating Condition A is significantly more willing to pay) and the purchase intent difference is at least 15 percentage points in favor of Condition A, proceed. Cost: 18000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home barista enthusiasts, leveraging premium positioning and direct-to-consumer channels. Recommendation: Invest in a differentiated consumer proposition targeting home barista enthusiasts, leveraging premium positioning and direct-to-consumer channels. Begin with a limited launch of a compact, high-quality espresso machine and build brand awareness through specialty retailers and social media. Target customer: Home barista enthusiasts who enjoy coffee at home for social and personal enjoyment, and who value quality and brand.. Value proposition: A premium, compact espresso machine that combines professional performance with a user-friendly design, positioned as the ultimate home barista tool for personal enjoyment and social sharing.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the proposed Consumer vs Professional Messaging Test to validate willingness to pay and purchase intent before full product launch.. Uncertainty: The long-term sustainability of home barista culture and consumer willingness to pay a premium for espresso equipment remain uncertain. The test will clarify whether demand is sufficient to justify investment.. Would change if: If the test shows no significant difference in willingness to pay between the two messaging conditions, or if purchase intent is low, the recommendation would shift toward expanding the professional line or maintaining the current portfolio; If new evidence shows a strong decline in home barista culture or consumer demand for premium equipment, the recommendation would shift toward a different strategy. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive the product as a premium, health‑enhancing solution that addresses specific concerns such as taste, safety, or convenience. Who benefits: Health‑conscious consumers who currently rely on bottled water or prefer a premium water experience.. Why behaviour changes: If Aquaporin positions its membrane as a high‑performance, easy‑to‑use purifier that eliminates taste concerns and provides clear health benefits, consumers will shift from bottled water to a single, reliable home unit.. How value is captured: Premium pricing for a differentiated unit, subscription services for maintenance, and brand extension into lifestyle segments.. Assumptions: Consumers currently avoid tap water due to taste or safety concerns.; A premium positioning can overcome these barriers.; Aquaporin can scale production and distribution to meet demand.. Predictions: Surveyed consumers will indicate willingness to pay at least 20% more for a membrane that promises superior taste and health benefits.; Pilot sales of a differentiated unit will show higher conversion rates than standard membranes.; Brand perception surveys will rank the differentiated unit higher than current offerings..

T2: Consumers will adopt a differentiated consumer proposition if they perceive the product as a convenient, low‑maintenance solution that reduces the hassle of bottled water or other alternative water sources. Who benefits: Busy households and consumers who currently spend time and money on bottled water, delivery services, or other water alternatives.. Why behaviour changes: If Aquaporin offers a membrane that is easy to install, requires minimal maintenance (e.g., cartridge replacement indicator), and integrates with smart home systems, consumers will switch from the hassle of bottled water to a single, self‑s. How value is captured: Lower upfront cost compared to premium membrane, subscription services for maintenance, and data‑driven insights that enhance convenience through smart home integration.. Assumptions: Consumers currently find bottled water delivery inconvenient or expensive.; A low‑maintenance membrane reduces perceived effort.; Smart home compatibility can be marketed as a convenience benefit.. Predictions: Surveyed consumers will rank convenience as a top reason for choosing a membrane over bottled water.; Pilot sales of a differentiated unit will show higher repeat purchase rates than standard membranes.; Pilot units will achieve higher adoption rates in households with children or elderly members..

Sample: 500 adult consumers recruited via panel, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region in Europe.. Measure: Percentage of respondents who choose the differentiated membrane over a standard membrane when presented with a scenario that highlights taste/safety premium (T1) versus convenience/low maintenance (T2).. Predictions: T1: At least 35% of respondents will select the differentiated membrane when taste/safety premium is emphasized.; T2: At least 35% of respondents will select the differentiated membrane when convenience/low maintenance is emphasized.. Decision rule: If the proportion selecting the differentiated membrane based on taste/safety premium exceeds the proportion selecting it based on convenience/low maintenance by ≥5 percentage points, adopt the premium positioning (T1).
